text:
sasha: Quick sync: we need a concise acceptance plan for Private Deploy upgrades + customer-managed networking. Key pillars: patch vs minor/major flow, installer choice for egress, and relay/BGP fallback.

matt: Sales wants near-zero disruption for patches. Legal wants clear egress handling for any relay option.

julio: Field input: two customers demand IP-preservation after upgrades and BGP sample configs; they sit behind NAT with asymmetric routing.

netops: Relay template minimal fields: `relay_host`, `bgp_asn`, `peer_ip`, `allowed_prefixes`, `tls_cert_id`. Relay must advertise customer egress IPs and be auditable.

kai: Acceptance sketch: 1) patch = hotpatch with canary and <1% error rate; 2) minor/major = bundle restart with rollback <=5min; 3) installer exposes `egress_mode` (direct_peer|relay) and records opt-out.

matt: Proposed default: hotpatch enabled for semver.patch, opt-out toggle in installer; add `force_restart` flag for customers who want deterministic restarts. Example test CLI: `redwood-operator upgrade --strategy hotpatch --canary 0.05 --verify ./checks/kv-check.sh`.

sasha: Launch gates: e2e green on aws+gcp+onprem, 3-customer 6-week beta, runbooks + rollback playbook, pricing/SLA for relay add-on.

deploy-bot: Staging: operator-v1.4.4-hotpatch smoke pass aws-us-east-1 at 2024-08-20T11:02:00Z. kv-checksum: ok, canary-requests: 1200, errors: 1.

julio: Action items: Sasha -> one-pager with acceptance + compat matrix by Friday. Matt -> hotpatch prototype + CI kv-check by next Wed. Netops -> BGP/relay template + compliance note by Tue.

Thread summary (sasha): hotpatch-by-default for patches; bundle restart for minor/major; relay-proxy fallback for non-peering customers; BGP/IP-preservation templates required.
